sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,711.76, near the top of its one-month range (7,316-7,799) - about 1.1% off the recent high. The Nasdaq-100 sits similarly elevated at 29,433.43 against a one-month band of 27,192-30,085, roughly 2.2% below its peak. The VIX has drifted to the low end of its own range, closing at 14.43 versus a high near 20.66 three weeks back - a calm tape heading into a heavy tech earnings week. Twenty-two SP500/R1000/core names report this week, concentrated in technology (16 of 22), with the rest scattered across industrials, consumer, and financial services.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Tue: PANW US reports into technology, sector median +0.4% off recent Q2 prints. Wed: AVGO US and BF/A US report the same day - Broadcom into technology (+0.4% median), Brown-Forman into consumer-defensive (-0.6% median, muted). Thursday is the week's heaviest day (15 reporters): DELL US reports into technology, while BN US (financial-services/alternative-asset-management, +0.1%/+1.6% median) and CPRT US (industrials, -1.4% median) round out a more diverse cluster.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the reaction table at +6.6% median across 160 tickers with a thick 2,626-item news window; oil-gas sits at the other extreme, -2.2% median across 33 names on 1,007 news items - also thick. Copper is a smaller but notable outlier at +2.6% median across just 6 tickers, though its 247-item news count is comparatively thin. None of this week's tech-heavy reporters sit in these three sectors, so the earnings calendar and the strongest sector-reaction signals point in different directions this week.
